children: , the integrated oil, gas and liquefied-natural-gas powerhouse, climbed 1.32% to 34.83 Monday. The stock outperformed a softer broader market as Brent crude pushed above $97 per barrel and escalating Middle East tensions sharpened fears of supply disruption.

Shell backed that momentum with formidable financial firepower. Its second-quarter results delivered $9.8 billion in adjusted earnings and more than $21 billion in operating cash flow. Net debt fell to roughly $42 billion, and management launched another $3 billion share-buyback program.

The cash machine is roaring, but the valuation already reflects plenty of confidence. Shell's $92.95 share price stands 13.84% above its GF Value estimate of $81.65, signaling that investors are paying a premium for its commodity-price leverage. Elevated energy prices can strengthen margins, yet conflict may also squeeze LNG volumes and inflate shipping costs. Shell's integrated network gives it more ways to profit from market dislocationsbut Monday's rally bets that higher prices will overpower the operational friction.

title: Shell Climbs 1.3% as $97 Oil Supercharges Its $21 Billion Cash Engine
